text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures continued their record advance to the 104-point level, with the trading mood described as good and a sharp upward trend intact. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.72, up 0.14 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended 10/32 higher on the day but a spate of afternoon profit-taking across Europe eroded much of the morning's gain. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-19/32, up 11/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures reduced their gains by the close after setting a new contract high of 132.94. The Treasury is to sell 22 to 24 billion francs ($3.8 to $4.2 billion) of new 4.75 percent 2002 BTANs on Thursday. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 132.68, up 0.32 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures lost early slim gains to register losses of more than a full point in late afternoon as political problems returned to dampen sentiment. Investors fretted over the government's resolve to deal with its budgetary problems and European monetary concerns while the lira slipped lower. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.62, down 1.05 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries edged lower in lacklustre late morning trade amid profit-taking ahead of January inflation data on Wednesday. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 113-24/32, down 06/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.55 percent.

JAPAN - Key March 10-year Japanese government bond futures ended slightly firmer with the downside underpinned by investor buying, including those with a remaining maturity of seven years. In after-hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.10, down 0.04 from the settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The European Investment Bank launched a 3.0 billion French franc 10-year bond, convertible into euros and fungible with an outstanding guilder issue. Otherwise the market was quiet with dollar deals still largely absent. DePfa launched 1.0 billion mark ($590 million) 12-year Pfandbrief at 35 basis points over bunds. NordLB issued a $200 million December 2000 bond. Ford Motor Credit Corp and Landesbank Rheinland-Pfalz were expected to launch five-year dollar deals. ($ = 5.748 French Francs) ($ = 1.703 German Marks)
